title: Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check
objectives: Apply the module's compliance rules to any MF/PMS/AIF recommendation.
Pass the trainer's final check: explain all three products, compare them on six dimensions, place a client on the ladder and judge each on its yardstick.
body_md:
Do: hold the right certification for each product (NISM V-A, XXI-A, XIX-A/B). Assess suitability, including lock-in tolerance, before any PMS or AIF. Sell AIFs only through private placement, to eligible investors. Show all fees, lock-in and tax side by side, in rupees. Disclose commission and the direct option. Advise clients to confirm tax treatment with their CA.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Hold the right certification for each product (NISM V-A, XXI-A, XIX-A/B) | Sell a product you're not certified for |
| Assess suitability, including lock-in tolerance, before any PMS or AIF | Treat the minimum ticket as proof of suitability |
| Sell AIFs only through private placement, to eligible investors | Advertise AIFs publicly or on social media |
| Show all fees, lock-in and tax side by side, in rupees | Quote best-case or pre-fee returns |
| Disclose commission and the direct option | Move clients up the ladder for higher commission |
| Advise clients to confirm tax treatment with their CA | Promise returns or exit dates |

> **Investor takeaway:** Mandatory line on all investor material: Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme-related documents carefully. All investor-facing material from this manual needs compliance review before it is published or shared. Final check for trainers: a new joiner passes this module when they can explain mutual funds, PMS and the three AIF categories in plain words; compare them on ticket size, ownership, liquidity, cost, tax and regulation; place a client on the right rung of the wealth ladder; judge each product on the right yardstick; and handle the myth that AIF and PMS always beat mutual funds.
